note: SOURCE CORRECTION. The IRW dictionary attributes all eight ecps_sahm_2024_* tables to Sahm, Burghart & Mier's German ERQ-S validation (doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/N26MB), with descriptions of the form 'German Version of the Emotion Regulation Questionnaire-Short Form - <X> Subscale'. That is wrong: the ERQ-S is a 10-item two-factor measure with no such subscales, and none of these item codes belong to it. The data are the COVIDiSTRESS Global Survey Round II. The ERQ-S OSF project does host Final_COVIDiSTRESS_Vol2_cleaned.csv alongside its own files, and its README points to osf.io/36tsd for that file's description, which is how the mix-up is explained. Every one of these item codes is a column of that CSV, which rederive_ecps.py re-checks. Three blocks are represented, carried as separate section_id values, and the table's own item_family column separates them 1/2/3 exactly as compliance / injunctive norms / descriptive norms. The three blocks ask about the same 8 behaviours in the same order, and the questionnaire words them differently for each ('Wash your hands regularly' for compliance, 'Washing their hands regularly' for injunctive norms, 'Wash their hands regularly' for descriptive norms), which is what assigns each block its wording. Position 7 is pinned independently: it is the one reverse-worded behaviour ('Met with people outside of your household for non-essential reasons'), and index 7 is the clear outlier in all three blocks, with a mean correlation against its 7 block-mates of -0.09, +0.11 and -0.04 against +0.25 to +0.60 for every other index. The wording is also corroborated by a second document: both questionnaire workbooks carry these blocks and agree word for word. option_text is left empty throughout, deliberately. The two questionnaire workbooks are registration-stage documents and their response designs do not describe the administered scales: they give information acquisition as a 1-7 slider where the live data run 1-10, and the agreement scales as 1-6 where the live data run 1-7 or 0-6. A '7 = Not applicable' reading was tested and refuted -- level 7 carries 37-39% of responses in all three sscd blocks, far too much for an escape option. Item codes ending _0neutral indicate a recode in the cleaned data file itself. No option label is asserted rather than guessed. The survey was administered in 47 languages across 179 countries, so no single administered language exists to name; the shipped text is the English master questionnaire and the language column is omitted rather than given a value that would be wrong for most respondents. The source file's per-respondent UserLanguage column is not carried into the IRW table.  The questionnaire's stated randomisation is visible in the data and confirms the block sizes: it says each participant randomly receives 2 of the norm behaviours, and the two norm blocks average n=3,794 and n=3,777 against n=15,081 for compliance across 15,607 respondents, a ratio of 0.251 or 2 of 8. Compliance was asked of everyone, which is why audit_batch.R flags the eight compliance items for a row-count anomaly -- it is the design, not conflation.
